subject: Error in dyn.load libpq.so.5 for rApache [ libpq.so.5: cannot open shared object file]

messages.author: 457700a8162dc4b2
messages.subject: Error in dyn.load libpq.so.5 for rApache [ libpq.so.5: cannot open shared object file]
parts:
I was establishing a platform with rApache + R + brew + googleVis +
RPostgreSQL。
OS: centos 5.5. RPostgreSQL are installed from official source code.

All was settle up, except RPostgreSQL.

Here, I have the following html, located in /var/www/html/brew/, named
as pgtest.html.
<html>
<body>
<h1>Colors</h1>
<% library(DBI)%>
<% library(RPostgreSQL)%>
<% library(RJSONIO)%>
<% library(googleVis)%>
<%
#setup db connection
db <- dbConnect(PostgreSQL(), host="192.168.0.80", port=5432,
user="postgres", password="****", dbname="bigd")
M <- dbGetQuery(db, 'select 1')
%>
<%= print(M) %>

</body>
</html>

[when i try to visit this page, the browser says this:]

<!--
Error in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...) :
unable to load shared object '/usr/local/lib64/R/library/RPostgreSQL/
libs/RPostgreSQL.so':
libpq.so.5: cannot open shared object file: No such file or
directory
Error : package/namespace load failed for 'RPostgreSQL'
Function brew returned an object of 'try-error'.
-->

[IMPORTANT!!!] It's not as simple as you see.
I fixed the error in R environment, by making a soft link for libpq.so.
5 to /usr/local/lib64, like this:
link -s /usr/local/libpq/lib/libpq.so.5 /usr/local/lib64/libpq.so
Then the R env can execute the sample database connect code.
BUT, rApache still failed!!!

anyone who knows the difference between R and rApache with regarding
to the library path finding stractery??

btw, i am not very familar with CentOS, so maybe some methods looks
like stupid, or errorable. IF you find this, pls let me know. thanks a
lot.

any respones is appreciated!!!

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: Error in dyn.load libpq.so.5 for rApache [ libpq.so.5: cannot open shared object file]
parts:
If you can get RPostgreSQL to work from the command line, do an lsof
-p on the R process to see exactly which libpq.so* is being loaded.
Scope out your LD_LIBRARY_PATH variable; figure out what's in
/etc/ld.so.conf. Once you have that info, then you can troubleshoot
rApache to see what's not getting set right. I do understand that some
Linux distros like to place apache in a restricted environment upon
startup, so CentOS may be doing that as well.

I know it's easy to softlink libraries as root to fix these kinds of
issues, but that's a rare case. It's always best to follow the distro
way.

Jeff
